In this paper we study the functions gk in detail. We also report on calculations of the
mean square of the L–function times a “mollifier” for each of the symmetry types described
above. The results on gk are summarized in the next section, and the results on mollifiers
are presented in the following section. The remainder of the paper is devoted to results
related to the various properties of the gk functions.
   We thank J. Keating, Z. Rudnick, P. Sarnak, A. Selberg, and N. Snaith for helpful
conversations.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Unitary families use absolute-square moments and recover zeta as a one-parameter family
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The unitary case changes V(z) to |z|^2 and B(k) to k^2, and reframes zeta's vertical shifts as a family, completing the three-way symmetry comparison.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Mollified mean squares distinguish symmetry types and reveal an O/Sp derivative duality
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The same inverse-Dirichlet mollifier gives different quadratic functionals for U, O, and Sp, including an anomalous short-mollifier orthogonal limit and the identity M_Sp(P,Q',theta)=M_O(P,Q,theta).

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Infinite characteristic-polynomial limits become finite factorial ratios, which admit exact valuation analysis and scaling limits rather than serving only as numerical constants.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Agreement with known low moments calibrates but does not independently prove the full L-function conjectures.
